subject: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls / rate limits & per-customer routing
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@fintechco.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 5 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls / rate limits & per-customer routing

Hi Alice 

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we all have the same record and next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

High-level pain & goals
- Need per-customer isolation and predictable billing: current system has noisy neighbors causing rate spikes and unpredictable costs.
- Want policy-based routing to route higher-tier customers to dedicated capacity to guarantee latency SLAs.
- Need rate limits, quotas, and soft/ hard throttles per tenant and per API key.
- Visibility: per-tenant metrics (tokens, latency, errors) and audit logs for security/compliance.

Current stack & constraints
- FinTechCo runs a mixture of microservices in GCP (us-central1) and manages keys in their KMS.
- Production model endpoints are hosted on a managed inference service today; they want to avoid vendor lock-in.
- Traffic profile: 90% low-volume users, 10% enterprise customers who each represent 40–60% of peak token volume.

Success criteria (what will make this project successful)
- Tiering: ability to define 3 service tiers (startup/pro/enterprise) with different routing and latency SLOs.
- Enforceable quotas: per-minute and per-day token limits by tenant + alerts on approaching thresholds.
- Failover: automated fallback from dedicated capacity to shared capacity with graceful degradation.
- Observability: per-tenant cost/latency dashboard and retention of audit logs for 12 months.

Specific requirements we discussed
- Rate limits: configurable RPS and token-based quotas, both hard and soft limits.
- Routing: policy rules to route by tenant attribute (tier) and by region.
- KV cache isolation or shared cache with tenant keys to prevent cross-tenant leakage.
- Billing tags on every request for accurate chargeback.

Open questions (asked on call)
- Do you require per-tenant model variants (quantized vs full-precision) for cost control?
- What are SLO targets for enterprise customers (p50/p95 token latency)? You mentioned 200ms p95	can you confirm?

Next steps
1) Ill send a short requirements matrix (attached) that maps features to Redwood capabilities and tracked gaps. (attached: requirements_matrix.xlsx)
2) Lauren will scope a demo environment showing per-tenant routing and quota enforcement.
3) Ben will follow up on procurement and a high-level pricing estimate for dedicated capacity.
4) You to share any internal compliance templates (SOC2 evidence) and the list of enterprise tenants to pilot.

Attachments
- requirements_matrix.xlsx (feature matrix we discussed)
- ftco_prod_arch_diagram.pdf (your architecture diagram you shared on the call)

Thanks appreciated the candid detail today.

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123
https://redwood.ai

From: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@fintechco.com>

Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@fintechco.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls / rate limits & per-customer routing

Hi Marissa 

Thanks for the great recap this looks accurate. A few clarifications:
- Confirming enterprise SLO target is 200ms p95 for token generation on enterprise tier.
- For model variants: we'd like the option to route enterprise tenants to higher-precision models; lower tiers can use quantized variants.
- For audit retention: 12 months is the minimum, we may need 24 months for some regulated customers should be configurable.

I uploaded the compliance template to the shared drive and included a list of pilot tenants (see ftco_prod_arch_diagram.pdf for tenant IDs).

Next steps from our side:
- I'll get the pilot tenant list and a short priority order to you by EOD Tuesday.
- Procurement will need a draft MSA and pricing to start internal approvals.

Thanks again looking forward to Lauren's demo.

Best,
Alice
Head of Platform Engineering | FinTechCo
alice.gomez@fintechco.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls / rate limits & per-customer routing

Great thanks for confirming, Alice. A couple of quick follow-ups:
- Lauren: can you confirm ETA for the demo environment (sandbox with routing & quota controls)? Target this week if possible.
- Ben: I'll flag procurement asks below so you have context for the pricing discussion.

Ben / Procurement notes to kick off internal pricing
- Pilot: 3 enterprise tenants routed to dedicated capacity (estimate: 2x A100-equivalent during business hours) + shared fallback.
- Requirement: configurable quota enforcement (per-minute and per-day), tagging for billing, and 1224 month audit log retention as a configurable add-on.
- Ask: high-level committed monthly cost range + per-token overage model.

Alice I'll send a short one-pager and a proposed time for the demo (Lauren suggested Thurs 6/10 at 10am PT). Does that work for you?

—
Marissa
